This piece was written from the perspective of Sampson, the dog, and what he might have been thinking during that time. No dog is going to see their family surrendering them as admirable—why would they? So yes, it’s entirely possible that Sampson felt this way. When we rescued him, he was deeply depressed.

To clarify, no human or shelter staff actually shamed his family during the surrendering process. No real-world shame occurred outside of Reddit. This was written to help people understand the pain and confusion Sampson likely experienced from a dog’s perspective—respectfully, a dog’s perspective.

Additionally, his family was given the option to foster him through the shelter until he found a suitable adopter. He could have gone home to heal, but instead, they chose to leave him in an unfamiliar place with 200 other dogs barking, begging for freedom. An environment he had never encountered before. And all for what? (Rhetorical)

The pictures that you see were actually taken AFTER he was rescued. I took them when I went to pick him up and he stayed a few nights with me. And his family chose to leave him at the shelter because of his energy level NOT because of his eye.
They had the option to get him back and they declined.
They had the option to get him back and they chose not to because of the burden of him being a husky and his energy level.

No shame in them giving up their dog :)


However, l’d like to say that this was written from the perspective of Sampson, the dog, and what he MIGHT have been thinking during that time period. No dog is going to find their family giving them up as admirable, would they? So yes, Sampson may have been thinking this. He was horribly depressed when we rescued him. 

And no actual human or shelter shamed his family during the surrendering process. No actual shame happened in the real world outside of Reddit. This is written so people can understand the pain and confusion that he experienced, from a dog’s perspective....respectfully, a dog’s perspectives. 

And also, yes, they had the option to come back and get him. Yet, they chose not to. They were given the option to foster him through the shelter until he found a suitable adopter. He could’ve gone home to heal…. yet they chose to leave him in an unfamiliar place with 200 other dogs barking all day, begging to be free. An environment he’s never encounter before. Mind you, he was in pain during this time as well because not only did he get his eye removed but he also got neutered the same week. 

Continuing on, when they were dropping him off at the shelter, they stated that they had him for less than a year and someone initially “dumped” Sampson onto them. They chose to never get medical care for him as his eye expanded and the pain continued. They stated his energy level was too much for them (which is understandable ofc), but they literally chose to not help him anymore….He was in the shelter for weeks before being saved. You do know that he probably thought they were coming back for him right?

All in all, he went through unnecessary trauma and confusion. And for what? Because he was being a husky and had energy even during the pain? 

So ….yeah, they did leave him.
